narrative.executive_summary: The goal was sulfide electrolytes derived from Li7P3S11 or beta-Li3PS4 that conduct lithium at least as fast as the parent and stay stable against lithium metal. The champion is Li6P2SeS7 derived from Li3PS4 with space group Pmc2_1. Its energy above the hull is -0.007 eV/atom with error 0.005 eV/atom from a mean difference on 25 known compounds of Li-P-S-Se. Its band gap is 2.485 eV and it is passivating against lithium metal with a stable window from 1.8 V to 2.24 V. Its diffusion coefficient at 600 K is 3.9e-06 cm²/s with error 9.6e-07 cm²/s, a ratio to the parent of 0.657 with error 0.211 and verdict tied. Its ionic conductivity at 300 K is an extrapolated estimate of order 0.1 mS/cm, namely 0.098 mS/cm with range 0.012 mS/cm to 0.8 mS/cm by own Arrhenius fit (500, 600, 700 K) with activation energy 0.421 eV, not a measurement. It shows interface reaction energy of -0.145 eV/atom with LiFePO4. Candidates that let framework anions move or that were non-passivating against lithium metal were excluded. Measured conductivity, DFT checks, synthesis routes, cost and experimental data were not computed.
champion_reasons: Its energy above the hull is -0.007 eV/atom with error 0.005 eV/atom, compared with -0.004 eV/atom with error 0.005 eV/atom for Li12P4SeS15 and 0.015 eV/atom with error 0.005 eV/atom for Li7P3SeS10.
Its energy per modified site is -0.115 eV per modified site, compared with -0.113 eV per modified site for Li12P4SeS15 and 0.323 eV per modified site for Li7P3SeS10.

Its stable window from 1.8 V to 2.24 V is wider than 2.28 V to 2.3 V for Li7P3SeS10, stays robust with maximum shift 0.02 V, and it has no confidence flag while Li7P3SeS10 has a window via a polysulfide flag.
tradeoffs: Its extrapolated conductivity estimate of 0.098 mS/cm with range 0.012 mS/cm to 0.8 mS/cm is orders lower than 5.658 mS/cm with range 1.456 mS/cm to 21.978 mS/cm for Li12P4SeS15 and 133.677 mS/cm with range 49.547 mS/cm to 360.658 mS/cm for Li7P3SeS10.

Its stable window from 1.8 V to 2.24 V is narrow and its interface reaction energy of -0.145 eV/atom with LiFePO4 indicates cathode reactivity, similar to -0.145 eV/atom for Li12P4SeS15 and -0.143 eV/atom for Li7P3SeS10.

Its diffusion ratio to the parent of 0.657 with error 0.211 is tied rather than faster, below 0.82 with error 0.251 for Li12P4SeS15 and 1.069 with error 0.23 for Li7P3SeS10, and its band gap of 2.485 eV is below 2.594 eV for Li12P4SeS15.
Its novelty is close family already studied, so it is a modification of known selenide-substituted sulfides rather than a new structure type.
uncertainties: Diffusion was sampled at 600 K with error 9.6e-07 cm²/s and ratio error 0.211, and conductivity at 300 K is extrapolated from 500, 600, 700 K with wide range 0.012 mS/cm to 0.8 mS/cm.
Stability relies on computed energies with error 0.005 eV/atom from 25 known compounds, and DFT checks were not computed.
Window confidence is limited by polysulfides including SeS7, with sensitivity tested to 0.025 eV/atom and maximum shift 0.02 V within limit 0.1 V.

summaries.text: Iteration 1 tested halogen-driven Li vacancies with dilute O passivation and Na expansion. Li5P2S7Cl, Li14P6S21O and NaLi13(P3S11)2 all passed the stability and insulation filters with energy above the hull of about 0.05, 0.02 and 0.01 eV per atom and band gaps of about 2.6, 2.5 and 2.4 eV. All three failed slow tests: Li5P2S7Cl showed framework motion with Cl diffusing at 17.7 percent of Li, Li14P6S21O showed framework motion with O diffusing at 5.3 percent of Li, and NaLi13(P3S11)2 was non-passivating against Li metal with a reaction of 2.44 eV per atom forming metallic Na. The agent concluded to limit halogens to one per cell and prefer larger Br or I, avoid isolated O in favor of clustered PO4-like units or isovalent Se, and drop Na mixing for non-reducible Mg vacancy or P-site As Sb substitutions, prioritizing dilute isovalent Se and As plus Mg-vacancy variants on mp-985583 Li3PS4.
summaries.label: iteration 1

summaries.text: Iteration two tested isovalent Se/As and Mg-vacancy substitutions to avoid Cl/O framework motion and Na reduction. Li14P6SeS21 and Li14AsP5S22 passed stability and insulation filters with energy above hull about 0.01 eV per atom and band gaps about 2.4 eV and 2.3 eV, and Li14P6SeS21 tied its parent for lithium diffusion at 600 K with D over D parent about 1.34 plus minus 0.34. Li4Mg(PS4)2 passed filters with a band gap about 2.6 eV but failed contact with Li metal because it forms metallic LiMg with a reaction about 2.27 eV per atom, so the agent concluded to drop Mg and Na cation mixing and prioritize dilute isovalent Se/As on Li3PS4 while avoiding Mg/Na and mobile Cl/O.
summaries.label: iteration 2

summaries.text: In iteration 3 the agent tested isovalent Se/As expansions on Li3PS4 and a single large Br substitution intended to keep the framework intact on Li13P6S21Br, correcting earlier Cl/O motion issues. Li3PSeS3, Li12As3PS16 and Li13P6S21Br all passed stability and band gap filtering with energy above the hull around -0.01 eV per atom for the first two and 0.03 eV per atom for Li13P6S21Br, and gaps near 2.4 eV, 2.3 eV and 2.4 eV respectively. Molecular dynamics at 600 K showed Li13P6S21Br tied with its parent with diffusion ratio 1.01 ± 0.20, confirming the intact-framework Br substitution fixes motion, and the agent concluded isovalent As/Se substitutions are the most stable on Li3PS4 and will submit the Se/As candidates to diffusion and Li-contact tests.
summaries.label: iteration 3

summaries.text: The agent proposed nine selenide-substituted derivatives of Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4 and screened them for stability, electronic insulation and lithium diffusion. Several candidates were rejected because the framework moved in molecular dynamics with chlorine or oxygen diffusing at up to about 40 percent of lithium, and others were rejected for being non-passivating against lithium metal with metallic decomposition products and reaction energies around 2.1 to 2.5 eV per atom. Three related candidates remained with near-zero energy above the hull and insulating band gaps: Li6P2SeS7 with energy above the hull about -0.01 eV per atom and band gap about 2.5 eV, Li12P4SeS15 with energy above the hull about 0.00 eV per atom and band gap about 2.6 eV, and Li7P3SeS10 with energy above the hull about 0.02 eV per atom and band gap about 2.4 eV. Molecular dynamics found lithium diffusion tied to the parent with diffusion ratios of about 0.66, 0.82 and 1.07 respectively. The agent concluded these selenide substitutions give computationally predicted stable insulating frameworks with lithium transport comparable to the parent but without a clear improvement.
